bugs: The global cases primary key used a signed-in worker id shared by every app. App-scoped lookups missed an existing other-app row and attempted a colliding insert.
Same-app concurrent materialization had a read/insert race whose loser rejected rather than adopting the valid winner.
Worker removal, form updates and durable post-effect patches reconstructed case ids from worker ids, preventing independent or retained identities from working.
resolution: Keep global primary key. Find exactly one app/Project-scoped commcare-user by hq_user_id, preserving all existing ids and closed/held records. New ids derive UUIDv5 from a versioned app/worker tuple, excluding Project. Primary-key retry happens only after CaseStore.insert own transaction has rolled back and only adopts the exact generated identity with matching semantic owner/type. Persona removal resolves the same row. Submission resolves one open matching-owner row before effects in its existing transaction and passes that actual id to durable caseDatabasePatch. Missing/closed/wrong-type/wrong-owner/duplicate identities refuse. No migration, compatibility rewriting, schema or public submission-wire change.
coverage: same signed-in worker, two apps in one Project and across two Projects with independent actual form writes and replay
six concurrent first ensures, exactly one created row, all promises joined and all calls fulfilled
legacy case_id=worker.id and independently identified existing row retained through ensure, legal pre-submission Project move and actual form write
same persona UUID installed in two admitted apps; removing one closes only its own row
closed row preserved; closed, duplicate and wrong-owner records refuse submission without changing stored rows
ordinary case whose id equals worker id is not a worker-record update target
